FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Plastics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 


Caprolactam [(CH2)s NHCO] is used in the manufacture of synthetic fibres, plastics, bristles, film, coatings, synthetic 
leather, plasticizers and paint vehicles. It is also used as cross-linking agent for curing polyurethane. It is represented 
by the following structural formula: 


О 


|| 
ЕС Сан 
/ | 
H.C CH2 
N / 


Oxidizable impurities in caprolactam constitute a critical quality parameter. From a study of literature, it transpired 
that this characteristic has been variously described as permanganate number, permanganate index, permanganate 
consumption or permanganate absorbance. 


This Indian Standard was originally published in 1987. In this revision, the major changes are as follows: 


a) Transmittance has been replaced with absorbance; 
b) Amendments have been incorporated; and 
c) Cross-referred standards have been updated. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex M. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and 
methods of sampling and test for caprolactam.

3 REQUIREMENTS 
3.1 Description 
The material shall be in the form of crystals or flakes. 


3.2 The material shall comply with the requirements 
given in Table 1 when tested according to the methods 
prescribed in Annexes. References to the relevant 
clauses of Annex are given in col (4) of Table 1. 


4 PACKING AND MARKING 
4.1 Packing 


The material shall be packed in either 25 kg bags with 
LDPE liner and covered with paper bags or as agreed 
to between the purchaser and the supplier. 


4.2 Marking 


4.2.1 The containers shall be securely closed and 
marked legibly and indelibly with the following 
information: 


a) Name of the material; 


b) Name of the manufacturer and his recognized 
trade-mark, if any; 

c) Lot or batch number in code or otherwise 
together with date of manufacture; and 


d) Any other statutory requirements. 
4.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this 
standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


5 SAMPLING 


5.1 The method of drawing representative test sample 
of the material and the criteria for conformity shall be 
as prescribed in Annex L. 


6 QUALITY OF REAGENTS 


6.1 Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be used in tests. 


NOTE — "Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.

ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. 1)] 
DETERMINATION OF PERMANGANATE NUMBER 


A-1 GENERAL 


Permanganate number is a measure of oxidizable 
impurities present in caprolactam. For this standard, it 
is measured as the time taken by 1 percent aqueous 
solution of caprolactam with 0.01 N potassium 
permanganate solution to match in colour with that of 
standard reference solution of copper sulphate- 
cobaltous chloride solution measured in seconds. 


A-2 APPARATUS 
A-2.1 Colour Comparison Tube (Matched) 


Nessler tubes with marks at 50 ml and 100 ml, 
provided with ground-on, optically clear glass caps. 


A-22 Constant Temperature Bath 


Capable of maintaining a temperature of 20.0 °C + 0.5 
°C. It is important that the constant temperature bath 
be protected from direct light. If a glass constant 
temperature bath is employed, it should be wrapped or 
coated with on opaque material. 


A-2.3 Pipette — capable of delivering 1.0 ml of 
solution (see IS 
1117) 


A-2.4 Interval Timer and Clock — capable of 
measuring a time interval of 120 min or more. An 
alarm arrangement is desirable. 


A-3 REAGENTS 
A-3.1 Potassium Permanganate Solution (0.01 N) 


Dissolve 0.316 g of the potassium permanganate and 
dilute to 1 litre with freshly boiled and cooled water. 
Clean glassware is absolutely essential for the stability 
of this solution. The solution should be stored in 
brown bottle and be prepared freshly every day. 


A-3.2 Copper  Sulphate-Cobaltous Chloride 
Standard Solution 


Weigh 3 g + 0.001 g cobaltous chloride (CoCl2.6H20) 
and 2 g + 0.001 g copper sulphate (CuSO4.5H2O) and 


dissolve in about 200 ml of water. Transfer to 1 000 
ml volumetric flask, dilute to the mark, and mix 
thoroughly. 


A-3.3 Double Distilled Water — of pH 6.8 + 0.1, 
conductivity less than 0.5 umhos/cm and silica less 
than 1 ppm. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Weigh accurately 1 g + 0.001 g of caprolactam 
and transfer it to one nessler tube, dissolve it and make 
it to 100 ml with double distilled water (A-3.3) and 
place in the constant temperature bath (20 °С). 
Maintain the water level in the bath approximately 2.5 


cm below the top of the tube. When the sample has 
reached the specified temperature (20 °C), add 1 ml of 
potassium permanganate solution (A-3.1). Stopper the 
tube, invert once to mix the contents, return to the bath 
and simultaneously start the interval timer and clock. 


A-4.2 In another nessler cylinder (see IS 4161), fill the 
standard solution (A-3.2) to the 100 ml mark, which 
serves as a comparison standard. Place this reference 
nessler cylinder also in thermostat bath at the same 
temperature (20 ?C). 


A-4.3 Measure the time in terms of seconds when the 
colour of the samples solution matches to that of the 
reference solution. Stop the interval timer and clock. 
Note the time in seconds. If the colour of sample 
solution matches to that with standard reference 
solution in less than 10 000 s, then report the actual 
seconds as permanganate number of 1 percent 
caprolactam aqueous solution at 20 °C. If the colour 
match is not yet reached after 10 000 s, the test may be 
interrupted and report the permanganate number 
greater than 10 000 s (see Fig. 1). 


NOTES 


1 Clean sample cylinders, and permanganate storage and 
handling equipment with concentrated hydrochloric acid 
(relative density 1.19) to remove residual manganese oxide. 


2 Remove the cylinders (when both the colours are matching 
within 10 000 s or requires more than 10 000 s and compare it 
to the colour standard by viewing downward through the tubes 
against a white background from which diffused white light is 
reflected.

ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. (ii)] 
DETERMINATION OF VOLATILE BASE 


B-1 GENERAL 

In the production of caprolactam, basic products 
(ammonia and organic bases) of volatile nature are 
formed, which have an unfavourable effect upon the 
degree of polycondensation as well as upon the 
process of spinning and stretching. 

B-1.1 Principle 

In a standard high efficiency apparatus, a known 
amount of sample is treated with alkali, and the 
volatile bases expelled are fixed up in standard 


sulphuric acid. The excess acid is determined by 
titration with standard alkali. 


B-2 APPARATUS 

B-2.1 Distillation Apparatus — see Fig. 2 
B-2.2 Wash-bottle 

B-2.3 Conical Flasks — 500 ml 

B-2.4 Measuring Cylinders — 250 ml 
B-2.5 Microburette — 10 ml 

B-3 REAGENTS 


B-3.1 Sodium Hydroxide Solution — 0.01 N and 
30 percent 


B-3.2 Sulphuric Acid — 0.01 N (see IS 266) 


B-3.3 Indicator 


Measure 28 ml of methyl red (0.1 percent in distilled 
water) and 7 ml of methylene blue (0.1 percent in 


distilled water) to a 100 ml measuring flask; make up 
to the mark with distilled water and mix. 


B-3.4 Pumice Grains 
B-4 PROCEDURE 


Weigh about 50 g of the caprolactam sample to the 
nearest 0.01 g in the kjeldahl distillation flask (4) and 
add a few pumice grains. Transfer 25 ml of sulphuric 


acid solution in a 500 ml conical flask (5). Add 8 drops 
of indicator and dip the condenser tube inside the 
acidic solution. Connect the assembly and then add 40 
ml of 30 percent caustic soda solution to flask (A) 
through the funnel. The funnel should be washed with 
distilled water after all the sodium hydroxide solution 
is transferred to the distilling flask (А). Start 
distillation by heating or by steam at a rate of 100 ml 
in 30 min. Collect about 200 ml distillate. Disconnect 
the apparatus, wash the condenser with neutral water 
and collect the washing in the same flask (B). The 
quantity of neutral water used for cleaning condenser 
and blank should be the same. Titrate the content of 
the flask (B) for the excess of acid with 0.01 N NaOH 


solution from microburette to colour change from 
purple to green (V2 ml). Every time carry out a blank 
determination without caprolactam to determine the 
content of volatile bases in same volume of caustic 
soda solution (40 ml of 30 percent NaOH solution) in 
the same manner. 


B-5 CALCULATION 
Vy —V2) XN x 1000

and

NOTE — Amount of NH; corresponding to | ml of

B-5.1 Report 


Report the result as volatile base in terms of meq/kg or 
volatile base іп terms of ammonia (mg/kg) (see IS 799) 
to the nearest 0.02 meq/kg or 0.34 mg/kg of ammonia.

of 30 percent sodium hydroxide solution through the funnel.

ANNEX C 
[Table 1, SI Мо. (iii)] 
DETERMINATION OF SOLIDIFICATION POINT 


C-1 PRINCIPLE 


A specimen of molten material in a test tube fitted with 
a thermometer is placed in an air-bath which, in turn, 
is surrounded by a water-bath held at 60 °C to 65 °C. 
As the molten material cools, periodic readings of its 
temperature are taken. When solidification of the 
material occurs and a minimum rate of temperature 
change (cooling curve) is observed, the temperature of 
that point is recorded as the solidification point 
(cooling curve) of the sample. In other words, it is the 
maximum temperature reached during a controlled 
cooling cycle after the appearance of a solid phase in 
liquid sample. 


C-2 APPARATUS 


C-2.1 Thermometers — with graduations of 0.1 °C 
and 0.5 °C, conforming to IS 2480 (Part 1). 


C-2.2 Stirrer — of SS wire of 1 mm diameter 
(see Fig. 3A).66 


C-2.3 Outer Tube — of heat resistant glass 300 mm 
length and 50 mm diameter (air jacket) (see Fig. 3B). 


C-2.4 Inner Tube — heat resistant glass, 200 mm 
length and 35 mm diameter (see Fig. 3B). 


C-2.5 Erlenmeyer Flask — 400 ml capacity 
C-2.6 Heater 
C-2.7 Asbestos Board 


C-2.8 Cooling Bath — Suitable container, having 
effective depth of at least 175 mm, shall be filled with 
cooling medium (glycerine 60 °C to 65 °C) 
(see Fig. 3C). 


C-3 REAGENTS 
C-3.1 Cooling Medium 


Technical grade glycerine shall be used as coolant. 
The temperature of the cooling bath should be kept 
5°C less than solidification point of the material. 


C-4 PREPARATION OF SAMPLE 


Take the portion for analysis directly from its 
container. Melt the entire sample by heating it at about 
80 °C, that is 10 °С above its solidification point and 
swirl it for homogeneity before pouring the portion. 


C-5 PROCEDURE 


Hold the cooling bath at 60 °C to 65 °C. Fit the sample 
container up to its lip into the cork stopper of the air 
jacket. Fit the thermometer and the stirrer into the two- 
hole stopper of the sample container. Adjust the partial 
immersion thermometer so that it is immersed up to its 
76 mm calibration mark in the sample. The bottom of 
the thermometer bulb shall then be about 24 mm above 
the bottom of the sample container. 


C-5.1 Clamp the assembly to the ring stand and place 
it so that the air jacket is immersed vertically in the 
cooling bath to a depth at which at least 100 ml of the 
length of the sample container is below the surface of 
the cooling medium. 


C-5.2 Allow the sample to cool while stirring it at the 
rate of about 60 strokes per min. The stirrer should not 
touch the thermometer or the wall of the sample 
container. Loop of the stirrer shall not pass through the 
liquid surface. Discontinue stirring after ап 
appreciable amount of crystals have formed but while 
the sample is still mainly liquid. 


C-5.3 Observe and record the thermometer readings at 
regular intervals, estimating degrees to the nearest 0.1 
°C until the temperature falls to a minimum, rises to a 
maximum and remains constant for essential period of 
time and finally begins to drop. The constant 
maximum temperature is recorded as the solidification 
point. As the temperature approaches this point on the 
rise, thermometer readings should be taken at 10 s 
intervals in order to make sure that the temperature has 
reached its maximum, and at least three more readings 
should be taken at maximum level, until the first drop 
in temperature is noted. Note the experimental 
maximum temperature, te. 


NOTES 


1 The accuracy of the thermometer readings can be increased 
by using a magnifying glass that assures a reading on a line of 
sight perpendicular to the stem of the thermometer. Also, for 
the record, the average temperature t,, of the emergent mercury 
column should be taken. 

2 If the temperature rise after initial crystallization exceeds 
0.5°C, remelt the sample by warming it gently in the sample 
container and repeat the test, seed with two or three small 
crystals of the sample when the temperature is 0.2 °C to 0.6 °C 
below the expected solidification point. As an alternative to 
induce crystallization, a chilled wire may be substituted in 
place of small crystals of sample.

ANNEX D 
[Table 1, SI No.( 1v)] 
DETERMINATION OF COLOUR 


D-1 PRINCIPLE 

The colour of 50 percent aqueous solution of 
caprolactam is compared with standard solution. The 
colour of caprolactam solution is a measure of content 
of impurities as it varies with the concentration of 
yellow coloured dissolved impurities. 

D-2 APPARATUS 

D-2.1 Colourless Nessler Tubes — 100 ml capacity 
D-3 REAGENTS 


D-3.1 Standard Solution — of 5 units, 10 units, 
15 units, 20 units, 30 units, 40 units 


One litre solution of 1.245 g of potassium 
chloroplatinate (КЭРІСІ;), 1.0 g of cobalt chloride 
(CoCLb.6H;0) and 100 ml of hydrochloric acid 
(specific gravity 1.19) in distilled water corresponds to 
500 units. 


D-4 PROCEDURE 


Prepare 50 percent aqueous solution of caprolactam 
and compare visually the colour of the solution with 
standard solutions (D-3.1) in two perfectly colourless 
and equal nessler tubes. 


D-4.1 Report the intensity of colour of the 50 percent 
aqueous solution in colour units. 


ANNEX E 
[Table 1, SI No. (v)] 
DETERMINATION OF IRON CONTENT 


E-1 PRINCIPLE 


Ferrous iron, in а dilute hydrochloric acid 
solution, forms a red-coloured complex 
with — 1-10-phenanthroline. The intensity of the 
colour is measured at 510 nm by means of a 
photo-electric spectrophotometer. 


E-2 APPARATUS 
E-2.1 Photometer 


Any  photo-electric  spectrophotometer ог filter 
photometer that can measure accurately the 
transmittance of the solution in the range from 500 nm 
to 520 nm. 


E-2.2 Dishes 


High silica glass, silica or porcelain, 50 ml and 100 ml 
capacity. 


E-2.3 Watch Glasses 
E-3 REAGENTS 
E-3.1 Hydrochloric Acid 


Dilute 1 volume of reagent grade HCl (specific gravity 
1.19) with 19 volumes of water. 


E-3.2 Standard Iron Solution 


Dissolve 0:100 0 g of pure iron wire (minimum 
99.85 percent iron) in 10 ml of H2SOq (1 : 9) and 
3 ml of HNO; (specific gravity 1.42). Dilute with 
water to 1 litre in a volumetric flask. One 
millilitre of this solution contains 0.1 mg of iron. 


E-3.2.1 Pipette 100 ml of standard iron solution 
(1 ml = 0. 1 mg Fe) into a 1 litre volumetric flask and 
dilute to the mark with HCl (1 : 19) (standardize 
with KMnO; for iron content). One millilitre of 
this solution contains 0.01 mg of iron. 


E-3.3 Hydroxylamine Hydrochloride Solution 


Dissolve 10 g of reagent hydroxylamine hydrochloride 
in 190 ml of water. This reagent is stable at room 
temperature. 


E-3.4 Hydroquinone Solution 


Dissolve 2.5 g of hydroquinone reagent or 
photographic grade, in 100 ml of HCl (1 : 200). Keep 
in a refrigerator in amber coloured bottle at about 
10 °C, when not in use. 


IS 12210 : 2023 


Е-3.5 1-10-Phenanthroline Solution 


Dissolve 0.5 g of 1-10-phenanthroline in 500 ml of 
water. 


Е-3.6 Sodium Acetate Solution 


Dissolve 100 g of reagent grade sodium acetate 
trihydrate (CH3COONa. 3H20) in 400 ml of water. 


E-4 PROCEDURE 


E-4.1 Weigh 100 g + 0.1 g of the sample into a high- 
silica glass, silica or porcelain dish. If the iron solution 
content 1s less than 5 ppm, use a mass of sample such 
that the solution on which the spectrophotometer 
reading is made, contains from 0.005 mg to 0.050 mg 
of iron. 


E-4.2 Place the dish in an electrically heated muffle 
furnace and raise the temperature slowly until the 
sample is completely charred. Then raise the 
temperature to 500 °C and maintain at 500 °C to 550 
°C until the sample is greenish white. This usually 
requires 4 h to 6 h but no harm will be done if the 
sample is allowed to remain in the muffle overnight. 
Remove the dish from the muffle furnace, cool to room 
temperature and add 5 ml of HCL (1 : 1) (see IS 265) 
in such a manner that any ash on the sides of the dish 
18 washed to the bottom. Cover the dish with a watch 
glass and heat just to boiling. 


E-4.3 Transfer the sample to a 100 ml volumetric 
flask, using water to wash the last trace from the dish 
and watch glass. 


E-4.4 Add 2 ml of hydroxylamine hydrochloride or 
hydroquinone solution, 5 ml of 1-10-phenanthroline 
solution and 5 ml of sodium acetate solution, using 
volumetric pipette. Mix thoroughly after each addition 
and make to the mark in volumetric flask of 100 ml 
with water. 


E-4.5 Finally, run a blank along with the samples to be 
sure that none of the reagents have become 
contaminated (see Note 2) and for a reference solution 
against which the transmittance of the sample is 
measured. Measure the transmittance ofthe blank with 
spectrophotometer, adjust to read 100 percent 
transmittance at a wave length 510 nm using 5 cm cell, 
when the absorption cell contains water. 


E-4.6 Measure the transmittance of the sample 
solution at 510 nm using 5.0 cm cell with the 


10 


spectrophotometer adjusted to read 100 percent for the 
blank. Read the iron content of the sample solution in 
milligrams from the calibration curve. 


E-5 CALCULATION 


Calculate the iron content of the sample in parts per 
million as follows: 


Iron, ppm = = х1 000 


where 


А — mass, in mg, of iron found; and 


B — mass, in g, of sample represented in aliquot 
used. 


E-5.1 Check Determination 


Make a single determination daily using 1 ml to 5 ml 
of standard iron solution (1 ml = 0:01 mg Fe) and 
proceed as described in E-4. If the determined and 
known values do not agree with the limits of 
experimental error (+ 1 percent transmittance), repeat 
the test. If the second result do not agree, prepare a 
new standard solution. If determined and known 
values do not check after preparing a new standard, 
investigate for errors in technique and reagents, and 1f 
none can be found, prepare a new calibration curve. 


E-6 PREPARATION OF CALIBRATION 
CURVE 


E-6.1 Pipette 10 ml, 20 ml, 30 ml, 40 ml and 50 ml 
aliquots of standard iron solution into 100 ml 
measuring flask. Develop colour in the solution as 
described in E-4. Measure the transmittance of the 
solution at 510 nm using 5 cm cell with the 
spectrophotometer adjusted to read 100 percent 
transmittance for the reagent blank. Using semi 
logarithmic paper, plot the percentage transmittance of 
the solution against milligrams of iron present. 


NOTES 


1 Platinum or platinum-rhodium dishes are not recommended 
as they sometimes cause a colour interference with the 
phenanthroline reagent. 


2 When the reagents contain more than 0:002 or 0:003 mg of 
iron, prepare new reagents and look for the source of 
contamination.

ANNEX F 
[Table 1, SI No. (vi)] 
DETERMINATION OF OXIME CONTENT 


F-1 GENERAL 


This method estimates indirectly, the amount of oxime 
in caprolactam up to 20 ppm. 


F-2 PRINCIPLE 


Oxime in caprolactam is hydrolyzed by НСІ to 
cyclohexanone and hydroxylamine. The latter is then 
oxidized by iodine to an equivalent amount of HNO». 
The nitrous acid formed is made to react with 


NOH 0 


+H,0 «HCl —Ə 


2 


NH;OH %21,%Ң/0 --) HNO) +4HI 


HO;S NH» + HNO, +H* — Н0;5 


I, +2 Na2S203 — 2Nal + N.S O 


acid to form diazonium salt. The solution at this stage 
is then buffered with sodium acetate, followed by 
removal of excess of iodine with sodium thiosulphate. 
The diazotized-sulphanilic acid is coupled with 1- 
naphthylamine, giving scarlet-red (violet) coloured 
solution. The intensity of the colour 18 measured using 
spectrophotometer at 520 nm and 
10 mm cell. 


F-2.1 Reactions

IS 12210 : 2023 


F-3 APPARATUS 


F-3.1 Flask — with ground glass stopper and Liebig 
condenser, capacity 500 ml 


F-3.2 Cylinders — graduated, capacity 25 ml and 
100 ml 


F-3.3 Pipettes — capacity 5 ml, 15 ml and 50 ml 
F-3.4 Volumetric Flasks — capacity 100 ml 
F-3.5 Funnel — 55 mm dia 

F-3.6 Microburette — capacity 10 ml 

F-4 REAGENTS 


Е-41 Hydrochloric Acid — 11 N, 32 percent 
(1.16 Specific gravity) 


F-4.2 Sulphanilic Acid Solution 

Take 10.0 g of sulphanilic acid in 750 ml of water and 
250 ml glacial acetic acid, and warm the mixture for 
the complete dissolution and cool to room 
temperature. Store the solution in dark coloured bottle. 
F-4.3 Iodine Solution (0.1 N) 

Dissolve 12.7 g iodine and 16.0 g KI in water. Make 
up the volume to one litre and store the solution in a 
dark bottle. 

F-4.4 Sodium Acetate 


Use special grade sodium acetate (CH;COONa3H20) 
stored in a dark bottle (see IS 557). 


F-4.5 1-Naphthylamine Solution 

Weigh 3.0 g of the compound and dissolve it in a 
mixture of 750 ml H;O and 300 ml of glacial acetic 
acid. Store the solution in a dark coloured bottle. 


F-4.6 Sodium Thiosulphate Solution (0:1 N) 


Weigh 24:82 g of sodium thiosulphate (Na2S203. 
5H20) and dissolve in water and make up to one litre. 


F-4.7 Standard Cyclohexanone Oxime Solution 


Weigh accurately 1.0 g + 0:000 1 g of cyclohexanone 


12 


oxime and dissolve it in water and make up to the mark 
in a one-litre volumetric flask. Concentration of 
solution is 1 mg/ml. 10 ml of this solution is further 
diluted to one litre. Concentration of the solution is 
0:01 mg/ml. 


F-5 PROCEDURE 


F-5.1 Weigh 10-0 g of caprolactam in the 250 ml flask. 
Add 15 ml hydrochloric acid (32 percent) and 40 ml 
water. Reflux the mixture with water cooled condenser 
for one hour. Cool to 20 °C to 25 °C (see Note 1), 
transfer the solution quantitatively to a 100 ml 
measuring flask and make up the volume and mix. 
Pipette 50 ml of this solution to a second 100 ml 
measuring flask. Add 5 ml of sulphanilic acid solution 
and 5 ml of iodine solution; shake well and leave aside 
for exactly 10 min (see Note 2). 


F-5.2 Add 9.5 g of sodium acetate and dissolve it 
completely, leave aside for exactly 10 min (see Note 
3), then add 5.0 ml of sodium thiosulphate solution and 
shake well. Immediately thereafter (see Note 4) add 
15.0 ml of 1-naphthylamine solution and make up to 
mark with water and mix thoroughly. Leave aside for 
15 min (see Note 5), and measure the optical density 
(light absorption) with photoelectric 
spectrophotometer at 520 nm using 10 mm cell 
(see Note 6) where optical density (light absorption 
value) of the blank (see Note 7) including all the 
reagents shall be measured simultaneously for 
adjustments. 


NOTES 


1 Temperature of the liquid in the case of oxidation with iodine 
influence the result. Care should, therefore, be taken to avoid 
a big difference in temperature from that at which the 
calibration curve is prepared. 


2 Time should be exactly 10 min as light absorption decreases 
with lapse of time. 


3 Time should be exactly 10 min to obtain the right light 
absorption. The light absorption value is influenced by the 
time elapsed after sodium acetate is added. 


4 1-Naphthylamine solution should be added immediately. 
The light absorption value is influenced by the time elapsed 
after sodium thiosulphate is added. 


5 The light absorption value continues to increase rapidly 
during the first 10 min after addition of 1-naphthylamine. Then 
the increase rate becomes lower. The tolerance would, 
therefore, be 15 min + 2 min. 


6 Distilled water should be used for the control solution for 
light absorption determination. 


7 Strictly speaking, pH of the blanks should be the same as that 
of the sample. Practically, however, any pH adjustment is not 
required because pH difference usually do not cause much 
difference in the results. 


F-6 PREPARATION ОЕ CALIBRATION 
CURVE 


Transfer 0 ml , 3.0 ml, 5.0 ml, 10.0 ml, 15.0 ml and 
20.0 ml of standard oxime solution (0.01 mg/ml) in 
different 250 ml conical flasks (add to each of them 10 
g of lactam with a small content of cyclohexanone 
oxime) and then add 40 ml of water. Then follow the 
details as given in procedure (see F-5), and determine 
the net optical density by deducting the blank from 
observed optical density.

F-8 REPORT 


Report the amount of cyclohexanone oxime present in 
caprolactam sample as the mg/kg (ppm). 


ANNEX G 
[Table 1, SI No. (vii)] 
DETERMINATION OF FREE ACIDITY OR ALKALINITY 


G-1 GENERAL 


The acidity/alkalinity of caprolactam is determined by 
titration using indicator. 


G-2 APPARATUS 


G-2.1 Erlenmeyer Flask with Stopper — 250 ml 
capacity 


G-2.2 Burette — 25 ml capacity with graduation 
interval of 0.05 ml 


G-2.3 Analytical Balance 

G-3 REAGENTS 

G-3.1 Sodium Hydroxide Solution — 0.01 N 

G-3.2 Sulphuric Acid — 0:01 N 

G-3.3 Indicator 

Measure 28 ml of methyl red (0.1 percent by mass in 
distilled water) in a 100 ml measuring flask and add 


7 ml of methylene blue (0.1 percent by mass in 
distilled water) and make up to the mark. 


13 


G-4 PROCEDURE 


Take 50 ml of distilled water in Erlenmeyer flask and 
neutralize it using one drop of the indicator. Weigh 50 
g of caprolactam into the Erlenmeyer flask and shake 
to dissolve it. Titrate the solution with 0:01 N sodium 
hydroxide or 0.01 N sulphuric acid as required using 
one drop of the indicator. 


G-5 CALCULATION 


VxN 
M 


Acidity/alkalinity, meq/kg = x 1000 


where 
V = volume of NaOH or H5SO, used for titration 
of sample in ml; 
N = normality of, NaOH or Н;5Од; and 


M - mass, in g, of sample taken for test 


NOTE — If the solution of caprolactam turns the neutral 
solution of the indicator red, express the result as acidity. 
If the neutral solution turns green, express the result as 
alkalinity.

ANNEX H 
[Table 1, SI Мо. (viii)] 
DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT 


H-1 PRINCIPLE 


The moisture in caprolactam is determined by titrating 
it with standard Karl Fischer reagent to an 
electrometric end point. 


H-2 APPARATUS 


H-2.1 Burette — 1 0 ml burette graduated in 0.05 ml, 
fitted with three-way stopcock 


H-2.2 Electrodes — platinum wire approximately 
25 mm long and 0.5 mm diameter 


H-2.3 Electric Circuit — a DC micrometer of 0 uA 
to 50 НА range and internal resistance approximately 
1 500 ohms 


H-2.4 Potentiometer — 
2 000 ohms 


H-3 REAGENTS 

H-3.1 Pyridine 

H-3.2 Oxalic Acid — pure 

H-3.3 Sodium tartrate dihydrate 
H-3.4 Gas Cylinder of SO; 
H-3.5 Iodine — sublimed 


H-3.6 Methanol — Anhydrous, containing less than 
0.1 percent of water 


with a resistance of 


H-3.7 Concentrated Sulphuric Acid — specific 
gravity 1.84 


H-3.8 Karl Fischer Reagent, Stock Solution 


Dissolve 85 g + 1 g of iodine in 270 ml + 2 ml of 
pyridine in a dry glass-stoppered bottle. Add 
670 ml += 2 ml of methanol (see H-3.6). Cool the 
mixture in an ice bath to below 3-9 °C. Bubble gaseous 
sulphur dioxide, dried through concentrated sulphuric 
acid, into the cooled mixture to achieve an increase in 
mass by 65 g. 


H-3.9 Karl Fischer Reagent Standard Solution 


Add 50 ml of the methanol to a clean, dry titration 
flask. Insert the stopper and adjust the magnetic stirrer 
to give a smooth stirring action. Turn on the indicating 
circuit and add Karl Fischer reagent in suitable 


14 


amounts. At first, the magic eye will remain open due 
to local concentration of unreacted reagent around the 
electrodes but will close as the reagent is consumed. 
As the end point 1s approached, the magic eye will 
close down slowly, after each addition of Karl Fischer 
reagent at the end point, the eye will remain open at 
least for 30 s. 


Add 1 drop of distilled water to the solution in the 
titration flask from a weighing pipette previously 
weighed to the nearest 0:1 mg. Stopper the flask. Re- 
weigh the weighing pipette. Titrate to the end point. 


H-3.9.1 Calculate the water equivalence of the Karl 
Fischer reagent as follows: 


F= 


зік 


where 


F = water equivalence, in mg/ml, of Karl Fischer 
reagent; 


W — mass, in mg, of added water; and 


T — volume, in ml, of reagent required for titration 
of added water. 


H-4 PROCEDURE 


Assemble the apparatus as shown in Fig. 4. Add 50 ml 
of methanol to the titration flask and titrate with 
standard Karl Fischer reagent to the end point. Stopper 
the sample inlet tube as quickly as possible to prevent 
absorption of moisture from the atmosphere. 


Weigh accurately about 10 g of the sample and add to 
the titration flask. Titrate the sample to the end point. 
Record the quantity of reagent used. 


H-5 CALCULATION 


CF x 1 000 


Moist = 
oisture, ppm " 


where 


C = volume, in ml, of reagent required for titration 
of sample; 

F — water equivalence, in ml of water per ml; and 

M = mass, in g, of sample taken.

ANNEX J 
[Table 1, SI. No. (ix)] 
DETERMINATION OF MATTER INSOLUBLE IN WATER 


J-1 PRINCIPLE 

A weighed quantity of caprolactam is dissolved in 
distilled water. The solution is filtered and washed 
through tared sintered glass crucible (G4). The crucible 
is dried and weighed again. The difference in two mass 
is the matter insoluble m water present m the sample 
taken. 

J-2 APPARATUS 

J-2.1 Sintered Glass Crucible (G4) — 30 ml capacity 
J-2.2 Wash Bottle 

J-2.3 Beaker — 2.5 litre capacity 

J-2.4 Oven 

J-2.5 Desiccator 

J-3 REAGENTS 

J-3.1 Acetone 

J-3.2 Double Distilled Water 

J-4 PROCEDURE 

J-4.1 Wash the sintered glass crucible (G4) with 200 
ml of double distilled water followed by 100 ml of 


acetone. Dry the crucible at 110 ?C in a drying oven 
for at least 15 min. Place the crucible in a desiccator. 


15 


Allow it to cool for 45 min and weigh accurately to 
four places of decimal (Mo). 


J-4.2 Weigh 1 000 g + 1 g of caprolactam into a 2.5 
litre beaker, add 1 000 ml of double distilled water and 
stir. Warm it, if necessary, to promote dissolving. 
Filter this solution through the crucible placed on a 
suction flask and wash the beaker with water. Wash 
crucible with 200 ml of distilled water. 


Dry the crucible at 100 °C in a drying oven for at least 
30 min. Place the crucible in a desiccator, allow it to 
cool for 45 min and weigh again to four decimal places 
(Mi). 


J-5 CALCULATION 


J-5.1 Matter insoluble in water, ppm = 
(M, — Mo) x 106 
M 
where 
М, = mass, in g, of crucible and residue; 
Mo = mass, іп g, of empty crucible; and 


М = mass, in g, of sample taken. 


J-5.2 Report 


Report the results in ppm of matter insoluble in water 
which is present in the sample.

ANNEX K 
[Table 1, 51 No. (x)] 


DETERMINATION OF ABSORBANCE AT A WAVELENGTH OF 290 nm (SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC 
METHOD) 


K-1 GENERAL 


Absorbance of aqueous solution of caprolactam is a 
measure of the degree of its purity. 


K-2 PRINCIPLE 

The absorbance of 50 percent aqueous solution of 
caprolactam is spectrophotometrically determined in 
1 cm quartz cell at 290 nm. 

K-3 APPARATUS 

K-3.1 Ultraviolet Molecular Absorption 
Spectrometer — fitted with a hydrogen or deuterium 
lamp. 

K-3.2 Quartz Cells — two, optical path length, 1 cm 
K-4 PROCEDURE 


K-4.1 Spectrometric Measurements 


Weigh accurately 50.0 g + 0.1 g of the sample, 
dissolve in 50 ml of distilled water and mix well. Filter 
the solution through whatman filter paper no. 40 or 
equivalent to remove any undissolved foreign 
material. Bring the solution to room temperature and 
let it stand until all the air bubbles disappear. Fill one 
of the quartz cells with the test solution and fill the 
other cell with water. Carry outthe spectrometric 
measurements at 290 nm, after having adjusted 


17 


the instrument to zero absorbance against water. 
K-4.2 Correction for Absorbance of Cells 

Fill the two cells used for the measurements (K-4.1) 
with distilled water and measure the absorbance of 
each cells at a wavelength of 290 nm. Let one of the 
cells read 100 since it has been used to adjust the 


instrument to zero absorbance. 


NOTE — The difference between the measured absorbance's 
should not exceed 0.003. 


K-5 CALCULATION 


Calculate the absorbance of 50 aqueous solutions of 
caprolactam as under: 


Absorbance of caprolactam (50 percent aqueous 


solution) — 21-20 in| cm quartz cell at 290 nm 
where 
A; = absorbance of the test solution, percent 
aqueous; 
Ao = correction for the differences in 
absorbance of the cells; and 
1 = optical path length of the cell, cm. 


IS 12210 : 2023 


ANNEX L 
(Clause 5.1) 
SAMPLING OF CAPROLACTAM 


L-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING 
L-1.1 Lot 


All the packages in a single consignment of the same 
size and belonging to the same batch of manufacture 
shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 


L-1.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the material 
to the requirement of this specification, samples shall 
be tested from each lot separately. 


L-1.3 The number of packages to be selected from the 
lot shall depend on the size of the lot and shall be 
according to Table 2. 


Table 2 Scale of Sampling 
(Clause L-1.3) 


SI No. Number of the Sample Size 
Packages in the Lot 
(1) (2) (3) 
1) Up to 25 2 
ii) 26 to 50 3 
iii) 51 to 100 5 
iv) 101 to 300 7 
v) 301 and above 10 


These packages shall be selected at random from the 
lot. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, 
procedures given in IS 4905 may be followed. 


L-2 PREPARATION OF TEST SAMPLES AND 
REFEREE SAMPLES 


L-2.1 From each of the packages selected according 
to L-1.3 draw small portions of the material from 
different parts of the packages. The total quantity of 
the material drawn from each package shall be 
sufficient to make triplicate determinations for all the 
requirements given in the specification. 


L-2.2 Mix thoroughly all portions of the material 
drawn from different parts of each selected package. 
Out of these portions, a small but approximately equal 
quantity of material shall be taken and thoroughly 
mixed so as to form a composite sample sufficient to 
make triplicate determinations for all the requirements 
to be tested on the composite sample. The composite 
sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one for 
the purchaser, another for the supplier and third for the 


18 


referee. These parts shall be immediately 
transferred to clean and dry containers which shall 
then be sealed air-tight and labelled with full details 
of sampling such as name of the product, name of 
the manufacturer, batch number and any other 
particulars of the consignment. 


L-2.3 The remaining portions of the material from 
each package (after a small quantity needed for 
composite sample has been taken out) shall be 
divided into three equal parts. These parts shall be 
immediately transferred to clean and dry containers 
which are then sealed air-tight and labelled with all 
the particulars of sampling given in L-2.2. The 
material in each such sealed container shall 
constitute an individual test sample. These 
individual samples shall be separated into three 
identical sets of test samples in such a way that each 
set has a sample representing each container selected. 
One of these three sets shall be marked for the 
purchaser, another for the supplier and the third for 
the referee. 


L-2.4 Referee Samples 


Referee samples consist of the composite sample 
(see L-2.2) and a set of individual sample (see L-2.3) 
marked for this purpose and shall be kept at a place 
agreed to between the two so as to be used in case of a 
dispute. 


L-3. NUMBER OF TESTS 


L-3.1 Permanganate number, solidification point, 
colour and absorbance at 290 nm shall be tested on 
each of the individual samples. 


L-3.2 The remaining requirement given in 3 shall be 
tested on the composite sample. 


L-4. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 


L-4.1 For each of the requirements (L-3.1) tested on 
individual samples, all the test results shall meet the 
corresponding requirement in Table 1. 


L-4.2 All the test results on the composite sample shall 
meet the corresponding requirement in Table 1. 


L-4.3 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the 
requirements of the specification if 1-4. and L-4.2 
are satisfied.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.:PCD 12 (18317).
